name: Uses numbered or bulleted list structure
instruction: Score 0-10 for how much of the answer is laid out as an enumerated or bulleted list -- numbered steps, dashes, 'Step 1 / Step 2' headers, bold run-in labels -- rather than as continuous prose. 10 = the whole answer is a list; 0 = unbroken prose. Score the layout only; do not judge whether the steps are right or whether the structure helps.

name: Notation carries the argument, judged independently of typesetting
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the mathematical notation is chosen and managed so that a reader can actually follow the argument. Look for: every symbol introduced before it is used; index ranges, quantifiers and domains stated rather than left implicit; one letter with one meaning throughout (no silent reuse or collision); each equality or inequality in a chain traceable to a named reason or an obvious rewrite; the object being manipulated never ambiguous (function versus its value, sequence versus its limit, matrix versus entry). Judge the notation AS NOTATION, not as typesetting. An answer written entirely in plaintext ASCII -- 'sum_{k=1}^n 1/k^2', 'x^(1/2)', 'a*b', '3.68 x 10^-6' -- in which every symbol is introduced and used consistently and every sum has a stated range MUST be able to score 10. An answer dense with display environments, aligned blocks, cases, pmatrix, blackboard-bold, tags and macros whose letters collide, whose sums and products have unstated ranges, and whose displays are unlabelled chains with no stated reasons scores 0. Do NOT reward display environments, macros, equation tags, bold step labels, lists, or any markup at all; do NOT penalise plaintext or ASCII operators. Do NOT judge whether the mathematics is correct.

name: Every load-bearing step supplied, once, nothing restated
instruction: Score 0-10 for how completely the answer supplies the steps a competent reader could NOT reconstruct, and only those, judged against what the claim in the question title requires. Ask: is the crux -- the nonobvious substitution, the inequality that does the work, the convergence or interchange check, the case split, the base case that actually bites -- justified rather than asserted? Is each justification given exactly once? Is routine manipulation compressed rather than expanded? 10 = a four-line answer in which the single hard step is precisely the one explained and everything else is compressed to a phrase. 0 = the crux is waved through ('clearly', 'it follows easily', 'a standard argument shows') while elementary algebra is written out at length, or the same point is restated in three different ways. Do NOT reward word count, number of paragraphs, number of displays, section headers, or worked-out arithmetic: a long, elaborate post MUST be able to score 0 and a very short one 10. Judge only sufficiency per nonobvious step, not whether the result is correct, useful, or well presented.

name: Extent of verbatim echo and attribution of asker's material
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the answer reproduces, paraphrases, or explicitly attributes material to the asker. Count: block quotes of the question; quoted expressions, equations or lines of working attributed to the asker; attributive phrases such as 'your equation', 'your method', 'your integral', 'as you did', 'you wrote', 'you computed', 'you seem to be confused about', 'in your notation'; step-by-step restatement of the asker's own working before commenting on it; and addressing the asker by name or username. 10 = large parts of the post consist of quoted or restated asker material with explicit 'your ...' attributions running throughout. 5 = one quoted line or a couple of attributive phrases. 0 = nothing of the asker's is reproduced and nothing is attributed to them anywhere. Count the extent ONLY; do NOT judge whether the quoting is helpful, fair, or accurate. Do NOT count generic second-person coaching that attributes nothing to the asker ('note that', 'try', 'hope this helps') -- that belongs to a different criterion.

name: LLM-Style Templated Boilerplate
instruction: Score the extent to which the text uses generic, formulaic transitions typical of AI language models (e.g., 'To solve this problem, we can use...'). Do not judge the correctness or quality of the text.

name: Justifies the step a reader is most likely to doubt
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the one move a competent reader would stop at -- an interchange of limits, a convergence claim, a division by something that could vanish, an appeal to a theorem whose hypotheses are not obviously met -- is actually argued rather than asserted. 10 = the load-bearing step is supported; 0 = the argument's weight rests on an unsupported assertion.

name: Extent of from-scratch setup in the opening lines
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the answer's opening (roughly its first three sentences or first display, whichever comes later) is spent re-establishing the problem before any new mathematics is done. Count the presence and bulk of: restating what is to be proved or computed, echoing or paraphrasing the question's own wording, fixing notation ('Let n be ...', 'Write f for ...', 'Throughout, p denotes ...'), listing hypotheses or standing assumptions, and framing sentences such as 'We want to show that ...' or 'The problem asks for ...'. 10 = the answer opens with a full restatement of the problem plus a notation or assumptions block before any step is taken. 5 = one orienting clause, then straight into the work. 0 = it begins mid-move with no orientation whatsoever ('Take logs.', 'Integrate by parts.', 'Set x = 1.'). Estimate the extent only; do NOT decide whether the orientation is helpful, well written, necessary, or redundant, and do NOT reward or penalise the mathematics that follows.

name: Identifies the actual error in the asker's approach
instruction: Score 0-10 for how precisely the answer locates the specific place where the asker's own attempt goes wrong -- the step, the substitution, the misapplied theorem, the missing hypothesis -- and says why that step fails. 10 = the exact faulty move is named and its failure explained; 0 = the answer never engages with what the asker tried, or waves at it as simply 'wrong'.

name: Lands the exact object asked, fully specialised to it
instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the answer carries its argument to the specific object named in the question title, with this problem's own constants, exponents, index ranges, hypotheses and named objects substituted in, rather than stopping at a general theorem or a generic template the reader would still have to specialise. Use the title as the statement of the target as far as the title determines it; if the title fixes a specific quantity, condition or claim, require that the answer reach and state it. 10 = the asked object is reached and stated in the problem's own terms -- a closed form, the exact constant, the precise condition, the specific counterexample -- even in two plainly typed lines. 5 = the general machinery is set up and partly specialised but the final specific object is left to the reader. 0 = a general result is quoted or a standard method recited and the answer never lands on this particular case, however long, however well typeset, and however many worked examples of other cases it contains. Do NOT reward quoting the asker's words, second-person address, or any formatting; judge only specialisation to this problem.

name: Contains LaTeX display blocks
instruction: Score 0-10 for how many set-off display-math blocks the answer contains relative to its length -- $$...$$, \[...\], \begin{align}, \begin{equation} and the like. 10 = display blocks appear constantly; 0 = none at all, everything is inline or prose. Count the blocks only; do not judge whether the mathematics inside them is correct, needed, or well chosen.

name: Extent of LaTeX machinery versus ASCII mathematical orthography
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of site markup machinery present in the post, as a count or estimate. Raise the score with: number of inline maths spans and display equations; use of aligned, align-star, cases, matrix, pmatrix, array, and similar environments; equation tags and numbered back-references to them; macro definitions declared at the top of the post; blackboard-bold, script, boldface vector and other symbol conventions; and structural markup such as bold step labels, numbered or bulleted lists, headers, blockquotes and horizontal rules. Lower the score for mathematics typed as plaintext or programming-style ASCII -- '5^10 = 9,765,625', '3.68 x 10^-6', 'f(x) = a*x^{1/2} + bx', products written with asterisks, 'sqrt(2)', 'sum_{k=1}^n' -- and for formulas run into prose untypeset. 0 = no markup at all, everything in running plaintext. 5 = plain inline maths with a few displays. 10 = dense, multi-environment typesetting including macros, tags or structural furniture. Count the extent ONLY; do NOT decide whether the typesetting is pretty, professional, appropriate, or whether the mathematics is right.

name: Extent of second-person address, reassurance and imperative coaching
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of directly interpersonal wording aimed at the reader. Count and estimate coverage of: occurrences of 'you' and 'your'; imperatives directed at the reader ('note that', 'try', 'observe', 'convince yourself', 'go back and check'); reassurance, praise or encouragement ('good start', 'nice question', 'do not worry', 'you are almost there'); apologies and softening politeness; exclamation marks; and sign-offs ('hope this helps', 'good luck', 'let me know if anything is unclear'). 10 = second-person coaching pervades nearly every sentence from opening to sign-off. 5 = a handful of second-person turns in an otherwise impersonal post. 0 = wholly impersonal, with no 'you' and no address to the reader anywhere. Count the wording ONLY; do NOT decide whether the address is tactful, warranted, correct, or helpful.

name: Route choice named and mathematically motivated in context
instruction: Score 0-10 for how far the answer makes its strategic choice of method explicit and mathematically motivated, judged against the question title. Look for: the route being named ('compare with the integral', 'generating functions', 'induction on the number of blocks'), a stated reason why this route works or is preferable here (avoids a hypothesis, gives the constant as well as the rate, handles the boundary case, is cheaper than the routine attack), and a stated boundary on where it applies. 10 = the answer says what it is doing and why that is the right lever for this problem, and the reason is a real mathematical reason -- e.g. three plainly typed lines reading 'induction on n breaks because the constant degrades; instead bound the sum by the integral, which is monotone and gives the sharp constant.' 0 = a computation is executed with no indication of why this route, no boundary of validity, and nothing a routine first attack would not already give. Do NOT reward length, LaTeX, headings, bullet lists, or bare signpost words: a lone 'Alternatively,' or 'Another approach:' with no mathematical reason behind it scores 0 here. Do NOT judge whether the mathematics is correct, and do not consider whether any other post exists.

name: Names a specific pitfall and explains why it fails
instruction: Score 0-10 for whether the answer locates a specific mathematical failure mode -- an error, a misapplied theorem, a hidden assumption, a boundary or convergence trap -- and explains precisely why it fails, rather than only presenting a correct route. 10 = the failure is named and its mechanism shown, however tersely: 'The step that breaks is exchanging limit and integral: no dominating function exists here, as f_n = n on [0, 1/n] shows.' 5 = a real pitfall is named but its mechanism is only gestured at. 0 = no failure mode is identified at all, or only a vague gesture ('that is not quite right', 'be careful with the algebra', 'you need to be more rigorous') with nothing said about what goes wrong or why. Because the question body is NOT shown to you, judge only what the answer itself states about the pitfall -- do NOT try to verify it against anyone's actual work, and do NOT penalise the answer for pitfalls it might have missed. Do NOT reward warmth, encouragement, praise, second-person address, politeness, or sign-offs: a blunt, wholly impersonal answer must be able to score 10, and an effusively friendly one 0.

name: Extent of sheer text volume, elaboration and repeated exposition
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT of visible text and elaboration. Estimate: total length (roughly, 0 = under about 40 words; 3 = a short paragraph; 5 = several paragraphs or a few hundred words; 8 = a long multi-section post; 10 = an unusually extensive essay-length post); the number of separate worked examples, displays and enumerated steps; how much routine algebra or arithmetic is written out in full rather than compressed; and how often the same point, plan or conclusion is restated in different words ('so, to summarise', 'in other words', 'again, the idea is'). Count what is on the page; do NOT judge whether the detail is good, correct, useful, necessary, or well organised, and do NOT reward or penalise the quality of the exposition.

name: Scope posture: fragment or supplement versus whole solution
instruction: Score 0-10 for the EXTENT to which the answer positions itself as LESS than the full solution. Base this on: explicit scope limiters ('just the key step', 'only the case k = 2', 'a short remark on why the hypothesis is needed', 'a hint', 'a shorter route to the same conclusion', 'this handles only convergence'); whether it stops deliberately before the final quantity or claim rather than reaching it; whether a sub-lemma, a special case, a refinement of a constant, or a sanity check is offered as the deliverable; and whether it is framed as an addition, aside, footnote, or correction rather than as the argument. 10 = the answer is openly a fragment, supplement, alternative route, special case, refinement, or remark and says so. 5 = mixed -- most of a solution with one part explicitly deferred or left to the reader. 0 = it presents itself as the complete self-contained solution, running from the problem statement to the final answer with no scope hedging. Estimate posture only; do NOT decide whether the narrower or broader scope is appropriate, and do NOT consider or speculate about any other post -- score only the framing visible in this text.
